# ts-diag and Diagnostic Workflows — Complete Architecture Guide

Standardized MongoDB diagnostic triage workflow utilizing ts-diag scripts to collect cluster topology, hardware utilization, system logs, and FTDC archives into structured diagnostic bundles.

## System Architecture & Invariants
- [HIGH] (core) ts-diag aggregates host-level metrics, rs.status(), rs.conf(), sh.status(), and FTDC chunks into a non-destructive compressed archive for offline analysis.
- [HIGH] (methodology) Diagnostic workflows must isolate whether latency regressions stem from WiredTiger cache exhaustion, ticket queuing, or unindexed collection scans before topology interventions.
- [MEDIUM] (antipatterns) Running collection-heavy commands like db.collection.stats() during high lock contention can exacerbate read/write ticket stalls.
- [HIGH] (patterns) In replica sets, ts-diag validates replication lag against the primary's oplog window size to prevent secondary sync failure during network partitions.
- [HIGH] (troubleshooting) Symptom: High network wait times with low CPU utilization. Cause: Socket queue backlog or connection pool exhaustion. Fix: Tune maxPoolSize and TCP keepalive.

## Primary Sources & Citations
- MongoDB Support Tools Repository: https://github.com/mongodb/support-tools (repo)
- MongoDB Monitoring Reference: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/monitoring/ (docs)
